issues: Scaled up from 480x270 design space, the numbers were about 40px and the dial radius 150, so the whole dial sat cramped at the top edge with the lower half empty
Pure white background, black text and an indigo last word, with no stage light or layout frame, like an unstyled test page
Compressed to 33f: a 17f sweep, 6f hand-off and about 5f per word, ending before it could be read, with no settle hold
The ending was a single 40px title line, weak as a poster and with no product information
changes: Paper look (warm paper, ink, vermilion) on a Swiss grid: drawn natively at 1920 with a 700px dial radius whose arc spans ~70% of the frame, 112px bold tabular Helvetica numerals, and a top hairline with SETUP TIME / HALYARD CLI 4.2 labels framing the layout
The sweep starts with a 5f, 3-degree wind-back, then a physical spring sweeps 99 degrees to 0 (a ~2-degree needle rebound, then a hard stop), with tangential motion blur on each fast-moving numeral

The dial has two more layers: fine ticks that turn with the dial (longer at numerals) and a vermilion needle at 0.35x speed; the static outer hairline arc and vermilion index stay on the poster at 35% after the dial clears

The 5 lifts off just before the rebound settles, travels 20f on an asymmetric in-out while growing from 112px to 150px, and lands exactly in the title's fixed first-character slot as the other numerals defocus in place
The 150px title '5 min to install' forms word by word through blur, 'install' turning vermilion as the only colour event, with a 40px mono command line '$ npx halyard init' below
Duration goes from 33f to 100f: a ~30f sweep, 20f hand-off, the sentence forming, then a 22f hold
